reason: Full-text proof plan: Monicity and O_K=Z[α] give O_K/pO_K≅F_p[X]/(F mod p); polynomial CRT identifies all primes P_i above p and residue fields F_p[X]/(g_i). To justify ideal exponents without the published general factorisation theorem, prove each nonzero prime localization R of O_K is a DVR by finite algebra. The monic minimal polynomial makes 1,α,…,α^{deg F−1} a Z-basis of O_K; Euclidean induction on this finite rank gives a finite basis for each subgroup and hence each ideal. For nonzero x∈O_K, multiplication by x has nonzero determinant, so O_K/xO_K and its localizations are finite. Thus each nonzero prime is maximal, and R is a one-dimensional Noetherian integrally closed local domain. Pick nonzero x in its maximal ideal m. The finite local ring R/xR has nilpotent maximal ideal; let n be least with m^n⊆xR and choose y∈m^{n−1} outside xR. Then t=y/x lies outside R but t m⊆R. If t m⊆m, the determinant trick makes t integral over R, contradicting integral closedness. Hence some z∈m has tz a unit; for every w∈m, w=z(tw)/(tz), so m=(z). For any nonzero ideal I, choose 0≠x∈I. Finiteness of R/xR yields m^N⊆xR⊆I for some N. Choose the largest k≤N with I⊆m^k; then I is not contained in m^{k+1}. With m=(z), an element of I with unit coefficient at z^k shows I=m^k. In the localized quotient by p, the polynomial presentation is F_p[X]_(g_i)/(g_i^{a_i}), whose maximal ideal has nilpotency index exactly a_i; in the DVR this equals the exponent of P_i in pO_K. Other maximal localizations are units. Equality pO_K=∏P_i^{a_i} follows by comparing localizations: any nonzero difference quotient has a maximal ideal selected from its finite quotient ring. All selections are finite; no Choice is used. Sources inspected: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 3.41 and proof, pp.62–63. Exact dependency IDs and hypotheses examined for the stated finite argument.
